# Wire formats (Anthropic, OpenAI, MCP) and benchmark action lists (tau-bench, tau2)

Fetched 2026-09-14.

---

## 1. Anthropic Messages API — `tool_use` / `tool_result`

A tool call in the Anthropic format is a **content block inside the assistant message**; the result
is a **content block inside the following user message**, joined by `tool_use_id`.

From [`anthropic-sdk-python/src/anthropic/types/tool_use_block.py` @ main](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/src/anthropic/types/tool_use_block.py):

```python
class ToolUseBlock(BaseModel):
    id: str
    caller: Optional[Caller] = None      # Tool invocation directly from the model.
    input: Dict[str, object]
    name: str
    type: Literal["tool_use"]
    toolset_name: Optional[str] = None   # For a toolset member tool_use, the toolset family.
```

From [`.../tool_result_block_param.py` @ main](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/src/anthropic/types/tool_result_block_param.py):

```python
class ToolResultBlockParam(TypedDict, total=False):
    tool_use_id: Required[str]
    type: Required[Literal["tool_result"]]
    cache_control: Optional[CacheControlEphemeralParam]
    content: Union[str, Iterable[Content]]   # Content = text | image | search_result | document | tool_reference | browser_state
    is_error: bool
    toolset_name: Optional[str]
```

Observations:

- **Arguments are a real object** (`input: Dict[str, object]`), not a JSON string — the opposite of
  OpenAI's choice below.
- **Errors are a boolean on the result**, `is_error: bool`, with the message carried in `content`.
  There is no error *type*. Guidance in the bundled `claude-api` skill
  (`shared/tool-use-concepts.md` / `python/claude-api/tool-use.md`, skill version 2.1.270): "For a
  failed tool, return `tool_result` with `is_error: true` — don't drop it."
- **`caller`** distinguishes a direct model call from one issued by code execution
  (`DirectCaller` | `ServerToolCaller` | `ServerToolCaller20260120`). This is the same
  "who invoked it" axis as OTel's `gen_ai.tool.type` / server-tool parts.
- **Parallel calls are a single assistant message with multiple `tool_use` blocks**, answered by a
  single user message with all the `tool_result` blocks. The skill is explicit that splitting them
  "silently trains Claude to stop making parallel calls". So *ordering within a step* matters and is
  expressed by block order, not by an ordinal.
- **No timing, no ordinal, no duration** anywhere in the wire format. The protocol records what the
  model needs to see, not what an evaluator needs to know. Anything temporal must come from the
  harness.

## 2. OpenAI — two different shapes

### 2.1 Responses API (current)

From [`openai-python/src/openai/types/responses/response_function_tool_call.py` @ main](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_function_tool_call.py):

```python
class ResponseFunctionToolCall(BaseModel):
    arguments: str      # "A JSON string of the arguments to pass to the function."
    call_id: str        # "The unique ID of the function tool call generated by the model."
    name: str           # "The name of the function to run."
    type: Literal["function_call"]
    id: Optional[str]   # "The unique ID of the function tool call."
    async_: Optional[bool]  # alias "async" — "Whether the function tool call runs asynchronously."
    caller: Optional[Caller]  # CallerDirect | CallerProgram(caller_id)
    namespace: Optional[str]
    status: Optional[Literal["in_progress", "completed", "incomplete"]]
```

And the output item
([`response_function_tool_call_output_item.py`](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_function_tool_call_output_item.py)):

```python
class ResponseFunctionToolCallOutputItem(BaseModel):
    id: str
    output: Union[str, List[ResponseInputText | ResponseInputImage | ResponseInputFile]]
    status: Literal["in_progress", "completed", "incomplete"]
    type: Literal["function_call_output"]
    call_id: Optional[str]
    caller: Optional[Caller]
    created_by: Optional[str]   # "The identifier of the actor that created the item."
    name: Optional[str]         # "The name of the tool that produced the output."
    namespace: Optional[str]
```

Notable: **two ids** — `id` (the item's own id) and `call_id` (the join key between call and
output); a tri-state `status` rather than a boolean error flag; and `name` is repeated on the output
item so an output is self-describing without a join.

### 2.2 Chat Completions API (legacy but ubiquitous — it is the shape most benchmarks store)

From [`chat/chat_completion_message_function_tool_call.py`](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/chat/chat_completion_message_function_tool_call.py):

```python
class Function(BaseModel):
    arguments: str
    """The arguments to call the function with, as generated by the model in JSON format.
    Note that the model does not always generate valid JSON, and may hallucinate parameters
    not defined by your function schema. Validate the arguments in your code before calling
    your function."""
    name: str

class ChatCompletionMessageFunctionToolCall(BaseModel):
    id: str
    function: Function
    type: Literal["function"]
```

and the answer
([`chat_completion_tool_message_param.py`](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/chat/chat_completion_tool_message_param.py)):

```python
class ChatCompletionToolMessageParam(TypedDict, total=False):
    content: Required[Union[str, Iterable[ChatCompletionContentPartTextParam]]]
    role: Required[Literal["tool"]]
    tool_call_id: Required[str]
```

**Arguments are a string, and the SDK's own docstring warns it may not be valid JSON.** That single
fact is why every downstream record format has to decide whether it stores the raw string or the
parsed object — and why OTel says "do the best effort to deserialize it to an object" rather than
requiring it. A record format that only has a `dict` field cannot represent a malformed call;
Inspect solves this with `ToolCallError(type="parsing")` plus `ToolCall.parse_error`, and the
Anthropic skill's guidance is "Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` — never do raw string
matching on the serialized input."

There is **no error field at all** in the Chat Completions tool message. An error is just text in
`content`, indistinguishable from a successful result.

## 3. MCP `tools/call` — spec revision 2026-07-28

Source: [`schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts`](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/blob/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts)
(identical to `schema/draft/schema.ts` on 2026-09-14). The 2026-07-28 revision is the current stable
one — announced at [blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/)
as "the largest revision of the protocol since launch" (stateless core, multi-round-trip requests,
`ttlMs`/`cacheScope` on list results).

### 3.1 Request

```ts
export interface CallToolRequestParams extends InputResponseRequestParams {
  /** The name of the tool. */
  name: string;
  /** Arguments to use for the tool call. */
  arguments?: { [key: string]: unknown };
}

export interface CallToolRequest extends JSONRPCRequest {
  method: "tools/call";
  params: CallToolRequestParams;
}
```

The call id is the **JSON-RPC `id`** on the envelope, not a field of the params.

### 3.2 Result

```ts
export interface CallToolResult extends Result {
  /** A list of content objects that represent the unstructured result of the tool call. */
  content: ContentBlock[];

  /** An optional JSON value that represents the structured result of the tool call.
   *  This can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null)
   *  that conforms to the tool's outputSchema if one is defined. */
  structuredContent?: unknown;

  /** Whether the tool call ended in an error.
   *  If not set, this is assumed to be false (the call was successful). */
  isError?: boolean;
}
```

with `Result` supplying `_meta?` and a required `resultType: "complete" | "input_required" | string`
(new in 2026-07-28; absent means `"complete"` for older servers).

The error-channel rule is stated precisely and is worth quoting in full:

> Any errors that originate from the tool SHOULD be reported inside the result object, with `isError`
> set to true, _not_ as an MCP protocol-level error response. Otherwise, the LLM would not be able to
> see that an error occurred and self-correct.
>
> However, any errors in _finding_ the tool, an error indicating that the server does not support
> tool calls, or any other exceptional conditions, should be reported as an MCP error response.

**Two distinct error classes — tool-level and protocol-level — and they go to different places.**
OTel mirrors this exactly (see `otel-genai-and-openinference.md` §1.7: `error.type = "tool_error"`
for `isError: true`, the JSON-RPC code otherwise).

### 3.3 Dual representation of the result: this is the key MCP design

`content` (for the model, unstructured) and `structuredContent` (for programs, validated against the
tool's `outputSchema`) sit side by side in every result. `Tool.outputSchema` is described as:

> An optional JSON Schema object defining the structure of the tool's output returned in the
> `structuredContent` field of a `CallToolResult`. This can be any valid JSON Schema 2020-12.

**Inference (mine):** this is directly applicable to Seahaven. An evaluator wants
`structuredContent`-shaped data (typed, schema'd, queryable by a judge); the model wants
`content`-shaped data. Storing both, or storing the structured form and deriving the text, is a
protocol-sanctioned pattern rather than an invention.

### 3.4 Externalizing large results

`ContentBlock = TextContent | ImageContent | AudioContent | ResourceLink | EmbeddedResource`.

```ts
/** A resource that the server is capable of reading, included in a prompt or tool call result.
 *  Note: resource links returned by tools are not guaranteed to appear in the results of
 *  resources/list requests. */
export interface ResourceLink extends Resource { type: "resource_link"; }
```

So MCP's answer to "the result is huge" is a **`resource_link` content block** — a URI the client can
fetch separately — versus `EmbeddedResource` which inlines it. That is the only size lever in the
protocol: **I found no size caps, no truncation guidance, and no pagination on `tools/call`
results** in the 2026-07-28 schema. (`tools/list` is paginated; `tools/call` is not.)

### 3.5 `ToolAnnotations` — behavioural hints that a counter design can use

```ts
export interface ToolAnnotations {
  title?: string;
  readOnlyHint?: boolean;     // "If true, the tool does not modify its environment." Default: false
  destructiveHint?: boolean;  // "If true, the tool may perform destructive updates..." Default: true
  idempotentHint?: boolean;   // "...calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments will have no
                              //  additional effect on its environment." Default: false
  openWorldHint?: boolean;    // Default: true
}
```

These are a ready-made vocabulary for partitioning tool calls into **read** vs **write** vs
**destructive** — exactly the partition a judge over a database diff would want ("the agent made N
writes, of which M were destructive"). Note the defaults are pessimistic: a tool with no annotations
is assumed mutating, destructive, non-idempotent, open-world.

## 4. tau-bench: the minimum viable action record

From [`tau_bench/types.py` @ main](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench/blob/main/tau_bench/types.py):

```python
RESPOND_ACTION_NAME = "respond"

class Action(BaseModel):
    name: str
    kwargs: Dict[str, Any]

class Task(BaseModel):
    user_id: str
    actions: List[Action]      # the ground-truth action list
    instruction: str
    outputs: List[str]
```

Two fields. No id, no result, no timing, no error, no ordinal. A "say something to the user" turn is
modelled as an action named `respond` with `kwargs["content"]`, so the action list is the *entire*
trajectory.

The environment appends every action to `self.actions` in `step()`
([`tau_bench/envs/base.py`](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench/blob/main/tau_bench/envs/base.py))
and errors are swallowed into the observation string:

```python
            try:
                observation = self.tools_map[action.name].invoke(data=self.data, **action.kwargs)
            except Exception as e:
                observation = f"Error: {e}"
```

The run record is equally thin:

```python
class EnvRunResult(BaseModel):
    task_id: int
    reward: float
    info: Dict[str, Any]
    traj: List[Dict[str, Any]]   # raw OpenAI-format messages
    trial: int
```

`traj` is just the raw chat messages — the structured `Action` list lives only in `RewardResult.actions`.

### 4.1 The database hash (relevant here only as a size/comparison technique)

```python
def to_hashable(item):
    if isinstance(item, dict):
        return tuple((key, to_hashable(value)) for key, value in sorted(item.items()))
    elif isinstance(item, list):
        return tuple(to_hashable(element) for element in item)
    elif isinstance(item, set):
        return tuple(sorted(to_hashable(element) for element in item))
    else:
        return item

def consistent_hash(value) -> str:
    return sha256(str(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
```

Grading compares `consistent_hash(to_hashable(self.data))` after the agent's run against the same
hash after replaying the task's ground-truth `actions` from a fresh load. Canonicalization is
"sort dict keys, tuples everywhere, then `str()`". The judging design belongs to the benchmarks
subtopic; what belongs here is the technique: **a canonicalized whole-state hash is one line of
code and collapses an arbitrarily large state to 64 hex chars** — at the cost of being all-or-nothing
and giving no diagnostic when it fails. Note also that `str()` of a Python tuple is not a stable
serialization across Python versions/types; this hash is not portable outside the process that made it.

## 5. tau2-bench: the same idea, considerably richer

From [`src/tau2/data_model/message.py` @ main](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/blob/main/src/tau2/data_model/message.py):

```python
class ToolCall(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default="", description="The unique identifier for the tool call.")
    name: str = Field(description="The name of the tool.")
    arguments: dict = Field(description="The arguments of the tool.")
    requestor: ToolRequestor = Field("assistant", description="The requestor of the tool call.")

class ToolMessage(BaseModel):
    id: str            # "The unique identifier for the tool call."
    role: ToolRole     # "tool"
    content: Optional[str] = None   # "The output of the tool."
    requestor: Literal["user", "assistant"] = "assistant"
    error: bool = False             # "Whether the tool call failed."
    turn_idx: Optional[int] = None  # "The index of the turn in the conversation."
    timestamp: Optional[str] = Field(default_factory=get_now)
```

This is close to a minimal sufficient record: **id, name, arguments (object), result (string),
error (bool), turn index (int), timestamp (str), and `requestor`** — the last because tau2 has a
*user* simulator that can also call tools, so "who asked for this call" is a first-class field.
`turn_idx` is the explicit ordinal that Anthropic/OpenAI/MCP all omit.

The task-side `Action` ([`src/tau2/data_model/tasks.py`](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/blob/main/src/tau2/data_model/tasks.py))
adds two fields that matter for judge authoring:

```python
class Action(BaseModel):
    action_id: str        # "The unique identifier for the action within a scenario."
    requestor: ToolRequestor = "assistant"
    name: str
    arguments: dict
    info: Optional[str] = None
    compare_args: Optional[list[str]] = None
    # "The arguments to check in tool call. If None, will check all the arguments."
```

`compare_args` is a **per-action projection of which arguments are load-bearing** —
`compare_with_tool_call` filters both sides to those keys before comparing. That is the
action-list analogue of "ignore the timestamp column when diffing rows", and it exists because
exact-argument matching is too brittle in practice.

The run container `SimulationRun`
([`src/tau2/data_model/simulation.py`](https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench/blob/main/src/tau2/data_model/simulation.py))
carries: `id`, `task_id`, `timestamp`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `duration`,
`termination_reason`, `agent_cost`, `user_cost`, `agent_usage`, `reward_info`, `messages`,
`trial`, `seed`, `mode`, `info: Optional[dict]` ("Additional diagnostics and metrics from the
simulation"), and `hallucination_retries_used: int`.

Note the counters that made it into the container: **cost (two of them, agent and user), duration,
termination reason, trial, seed** — and a generic `info` dict for everything else. Again: **no
per-tool call counts.**

## 6. Side-by-side: what a "tool call record" contains across seven sources

| | id | name | args type | result | error | ordinal | timing | who called |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OTel `execute_tool` span | `gen_ai.tool.call.id` | `gen_ai.tool.name` | object (opt-in) | opt-in attr | `error.type` (low-card string) | implicit (trace) | span start/end | `gen_ai.tool.type`, `gen_ai.agent.name` |
| OpenInference `TOOL` span | `tool.id` / `tool_call.id` | `tool.name` | **JSON string** | `output.value` | span status only | flattened index | span start/end | — |
| Inspect `ToolEvent` | `id`, `uuid` | `function` | object | `result` + `truncated` | `ToolCallError{type,message}` + `failed` | list order, `span_id` | `timestamp`, `completed`, `working_time` | `agent`, `agent_span_id` |
| LangSmith `Run` | `id` | `name` | `inputs: dict` | `outputs: dict` | `error: str` | `dotted_order` | `start_time`, `end_time` | `parent_run_id` |
| Anthropic blocks | `id` / `tool_use_id` | `name` | object (`input`) | `content` | `is_error: bool` | block order | — | `caller` |
| OpenAI Responses | `id` + `call_id` | `name` | **JSON string** | `output` | `status` tri-state | item order | — | `caller` |
| MCP `tools/call` | JSON-RPC `id` | `params.name` | object | `content` + `structuredContent` | `isError: bool` (+ JSON-RPC error) | — | — | — |
| tau2 `ToolCall`/`ToolMessage` | `id` | `name` | object | `content: str` | `error: bool` | `turn_idx` | `timestamp` | `requestor` |

**Every source has name + arguments + a join id. Nothing else is universal.** Errors are modelled
four different ways (typed enum, boolean, tri-state status, free string). Timing is present in three
of eight. An explicit ordinal is present in two of eight.
